backlog: Pilot #3 security finding: API echoed any Origin
context: Eight routes carry a bare @cross_origin(). In flask-cors 6.0.5 it does two things: it replaces the app-wide origin allow-list with defaults (any origin, echoed) AND it answers OPTIONS preflights before the view runs. Verified 2026-10-02 against the REAL app.py in the real image: all 8 preflights return 200 with ACAO echoing https://evil.example.

Rev 1 removed only the decorators. Kiro's run showed (flask 3.1.3, flask-cors 6.0.5) that routes listing 'OPTIONS' without an OPTIONS branch then run the view on preflights: messages GET 401, messages POST 415, reply 401, profile update 415. Browsers reject non-2xx preflights. Credit: Kiro, rev 1 report.

Rev 2: remove all 8 decorators; on the 5 routes whose views have no OPTIONS branch (messages GET, messages POST, home, reply, profile update) also drop 'OPTIONS' from methods so Flask answers OPTIONS itself (the way /api/message_groups already works). /api/activities and /api/users keep 'OPTIONS' because their views return 204 for it. Replies is GET-only already.

bin/cors-probe is new: it imports the real working-tree app.py inside the pinned backend image with networking off and checks every preflight's STATUS and headers. C runs it as the acceptance test (operator gate) before committing. Kiro must not run it.
Commits do not deploy. This reaches the site in pilot #4.
must_not: No git add, commit, push, stash, reset, restore, checkout, rebase or history change. C commits.
No AWS CLI, no docker, no running anything under bin/ (including the new bin/cors-probe), no pip/npm installs, no throwaway venvs.
No edits outside files_in_scope. Do not change route bodies, the app-wide CORS(...) block or after_request.
Use IDE tools for every edit and for creating bin/cors-probe; never write files through a shell command. Do not chmod (C does it).
Apply each edit exactly as given; no other cleanup.

create.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bin/cors-probe — run the WORKING-TREE backend-flask/app.py inside the pinned
# backend image (network off) and send a CORS preflight to every browser-called
# /api route, from the real site and from https://evil.example.
#   PASS = real site gets a 2xx with its own origin and "authorization" allowed;
#          evil.example gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header at all.
# Read-only: the source is mounted :ro and the container is removed afterwards.
# Usage: ./bin/cors-probe [image]
#   default image = EcrImage in aws/cfn/service/config.toml
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

IMAGE="${1:-$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*EcrImage[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"].*/\1/p" aws/cfn/service/config.toml 2>/dev/null)}"
if [ -z "$IMAGE" ]; then
  echo "No image given and no EcrImage line in aws/cfn/service/config.toml" >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "Image: $IMAGE"

LOG="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$LOG"' EXIT

set +e
docker run --rm -i --network none -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  -e FRONTEND_URL=https://fentoncruddur.com -e BACKEND_URL=https://api.fentoncruddur.com \
  -e AWS_REGION=us-east-1 -e AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 \
  -e CONNECTION_URL=postgresql://x:x@127.0.0.1:5432/x \
  -e AWS_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID=us-east-1_dummy -e AWS_COGNITO_USER_POOL_CLIENT_ID=dummy \
  -v "$PWD/backend-flask:/backend-flask:ro" -w /backend-flask \
  --entrypoint python3 "$IMAGE" - > "$LOG" 2>&1 <<'PY'
import sys, importlib.metadata as m, requests

class FakeResp:
    status_code = 200
    def json(self): return {"keys": []}
    def raise_for_status(self): pass
# Network is off. The token checker downloads Cognito's JWKS at import time;
# give it an empty key list. Preflights never verify a token.
requests.get = lambda *a, **k: FakeResp()

sys.path.insert(0, "/backend-flask")
import app as real
c = real.app.test_client()
GOOD, EVIL = "https://fentoncruddur.com", "https://evil.example"
routes = [("/api/message_groups", "GET"), ("/api/messages/abc", "GET"), ("/api/messages", "POST"),
          ("/api/activities/home", "GET"), ("/api/activities", "POST"),
          ("/api/activities/abc/replies", "GET"), ("/api/activities/abc/reply", "POST"),
          ("/api/users", "GET"), ("/api/profile/update", "POST")]
print("PROBE flask", m.version("flask"), "flask-cors", m.version("flask-cors"))
ok = True
for path, meth in routes:
    for origin in (GOOD, EVIL):
        r = c.open(path, method="OPTIONS", headers={
            "Origin": origin, "Access-Control-Request-Method": meth,
            "Access-Control-Request-Headers": "authorization,content-type"})
        acao = r.headers.get("Access-Control-Allow-Origin")
        acah = (r.headers.get("Access-Control-Allow-Headers") or "").lower()
        if origin == GOOD:
            good = 200 <= r.status_code < 300 and acao == GOOD and "authorization" in acah
        else:
            good = acao is None
        ok = ok and good
        print(f"PROBE {'ok  ' if good else 'FAIL'} {meth:4} {path:28} {origin:26} {r.status_code} ACAO={acao}")
r = c.get("/api/activities/home", headers={"Origin": EVIL})
good = r.headers.get("Access-Control-Allow-Origin") is None
ok = ok and good
print(f"PROBE {'ok  ' if good else 'FAIL'} GET  /api/activities/home (simple) {EVIL:26} {r.status_code} ACAO={r.headers.get('Access-Control-Allow-Origin')}")
print("PROBE RESULT:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY
rc=$?
set -e

grep '^PROBE' "$LOG" || true
if ! grep -q '^PROBE RESULT' "$LOG"; then
  echo "--- the probe did not finish; last lines of output:"
  tail -20 "$LOG"
  exit 2
fi
exit $rc
